I am an old woman, seventy-one years, and this small piece of land near my house is all I have — less than a quarter acre. Here in Dodoma the rains are little and they come late, so I do not waste money on fertilizer from the shop — one bag costs too much for my small plot, and if the rains fail the money is gone. I use the manure from my few goats and chickens, and I keep the seeds I saved from last harvest like my mother taught me. My children help me when they can, but mostly I work it myself with my hoe, slowly, the way I know.
